claims.evidence: Photo 0 and 1 show the hardware design and logos consistent with an original Xbox One console.
Photo 1 shows one black wireless controller.
No games or digital library screens are shown in the report.
The witness cannot verify power issues without testing the unit with a known good power supply.
The warranty seals on the rear of the console are not shown.
Requires the console to be running under load for an extended period.
The rear connection ports are not shown in the report.
No documentation or receipts are shown in the photos.

risks.risk: The 'adaptor issue' may actually be a failure of the internal power IC or motherboard.
risks.proof: A video of the console booting to the home dashboard using a working power supply.
risks.if_unproven: as a non-working unit for parts only.

risks.risk: The disc drive may be unable to read or eject discs.
risks.proof: A video showing a disc being inserted, recognized by the system, and launched.
risks.if_unproven: as a 'digital only' console with a broken drive.

risks.risk: The controller may have stick drift or unresponsive buttons.
risks.proof: A video of the controller being used in the 'Xbox Accessories' app test mode.
risks.if_unproven: as a console without a working controller.

risks.risk: The console may have the base 500GB storage rather than the 1TB version.
risks.proof: A photo of the 'Storage' section in the System Settings menu.

proof_requests: Video of the console powering on and reaching the home screen.
Photo of the rear of the console showing the warranty seal and ports.
Photo of the 'About' or 'Storage' screen in settings.
Photo of the 6 physical game discs or the digital library.
Photo of the UK receipt mentioned.
response.reason: The item is clearly identified as an original Xbox One, but the seller's admission of a power issue without proof of life requires it to be priced at the lowest possible value for a non-functional unit.
